name: Hearthpatch Elder's Walking Coat Set
description: Not every Shelf outfit is built for running or hiding. This one is built for endurance, dignity, and the long walk. The centerpiece is a full-length coat — originally a women's overcoat in deep burgundy wool, now faded to a dusty maroon with a gray undertone — that has been repaired so many times it has become a new garment. Every patch is a different fabric: a square of dark green canvas at the left elbow, a strip of black synthrubber at the hem where puddle-rot set in, a careful re-weaving of the right lapel with rust-colored thread that doesn't quite match but holds the shape. The coat falls to mid-calf and is belted with a wide leather strap, worn and darkened with age, the original buckle replaced with a hand-bent wire clasp. Beneath it, a layered situation: a thick ribbed turtleneck in off-white that's been washed gray, tucked into wide-leg trousers in dark brown heavy cotton, the waistband reinforced with a second strip of fabric sewn over the original. Shoes are flat, wide-last, in cracked dark leather resoled twice in thick rubber — the kind of shoe built for someone who stands and walks all day and needs their feet to still work at the end of it. A wide wool headwrap in faded teal and rust, gene-compatible in its generous size and soft drape, covers the head and wraps loosely at the neck. Hands are bare. The coat's interior has been fitted with four hand-sewn pockets, deep and flat, invisible from outside.
functionality: Full-length coat provides exceptional cold and wind protection across the Shelf's exposed corridors. Multiple interior pockets distribute weight and keep valuables close to the body and out of view. Wide-last resoled shoes support long-duration walking on uneven Shelf terrain. Wool headwrap provides warmth and can be repositioned as a face cover. Gene-compatible headwrap accommodates horns or cranial geneware without adjustment.
what_it_says: Age, survival, and the particular pride of someone who refuses to look defeated. Every repair in this coat is a year of living on the Shelf, and the wearer wears them all openly. This is not someone who dresses down — this is someone who dresses with everything they have, and everything they have is a coat that's been loved back from the dead.
worn_by: anyone who has been on the Shelf long enough to develop style instead of just survival
manufacturer: Coat is of unknown original manufacture, extensively self-repaired over years; all other components are Shelf market or self-made
price_range: Φ8–Φ22 (the coat is priceless to the wearer)
story_hooks: Sewn into the lining of the coat, between two older patches, is a folded document — something the wearer either forgot was there or is deliberately carrying without acknowledging.
A Tier 3 vintage textile dealer spots the original coat's construction and realizes it's pre-Collapse manufacture, potentially worth far more than the wearer could imagine — and wants it badly.
The wire clasp on the belt is a specific design that functions as a recognition signal among a Shelf mutual-aid network — and a newcomer who knows the signal is desperately trying to make contact.
